issue_294_text: planner identifies a unit completely solvable/verifiable by an existing/new deterministic mechanism and does not spend an unnecessary reasoning-worker call on that unit
status: demonstrated via constructed exercise, structural-eligibility scope only (see documented_trust_boundary below), after a seven-round correction sequence -- see history below
history: Round 0 (original, invalid; PR #393): pointed at real #294 units 294-B and 294-C, whose own 'Files/surfaces expected to change' fields name the very scripts each unit was itself building. Stage 2 audit #396 (on PR #393's merge) found this was never actually the right example -- it depended on a routing bug (own-deliverable scripts wrongly treated as deterministically satisfied) fixed in that same PR's `isUnitsOwnDeliverable`.

Round 1 (invalid; PR #399): a synthetic unit's 'Required bounded outcome' required producing a second, unrelated documentation deliverable that the invoked gate script (ready-dispatch-gate.mjs) cannot produce -- a false-positive route that left the unit's real outcome unfinished (Stage 1 review finding on PR #399, fixed in the same PR).

Round 2 (invalid; PR #401, first attempt): a synthetic unit named the invoked script in 'Files/surfaces expected to change' while separately asserting in prose that the script was 'not modified' -- an internally contradictory contract, since that field's own name asserts the opposite (Stage 2 audit #400, P1, on PR #399's merge). Fixing this exposed the real, underlying defect in `resolveUnitRoute` itself: it inferred 'genuine pre-existing mechanism' merely from a script's existence-on-disk plus textual absence from 'Required bounded outcome' -- unsound whenever a valid contract's outcome paraphrases the same file without quoting its exact backtick path (Stage 1 review finding on PR #401).

Round 3 (partially valid, incomplete; PR #401, fixed in the same PR): `resolveUnitRoute` gained an explicit, fixed annotation requirement -- '(invoked, not modified)' -- immediately after a script's own backtick-quoted path in 'Files/surfaces expected to change' before that entry was eligible for the deterministic-script route at all. This closed the truthfulness gap from Round 2 and let the constructed exercise be rebuilt non-contradictorily. PR #401 merged with this fix. Stage 2 audit #402 (on PR #401's merge) then found it incomplete: the annotation protected only the ONE annotated entry, not the unit's whole outcome. A unit whose Files/surfaces named an annotated, genuinely pre-existing script ALONGSIDE a separate, real deliverable was still wrongly routed to 'just run the annotated script', silently leaving the separate deliverable unimplemented -- reproducing the Round 1/2 class of defect via a different field shape.

Round 4 (invalid, superseded; PR #403, first commit): added a check that the annotated script be the ONLY backtick code span named in the field. PR #403's own Stage 1 review found this incomplete in two directions at once: (a) the parser does not require backtick-quoting for this field, so a second surface named in PLAIN, unquoted text was invisible to a code-span count -- the same unsatisfied-outcome defect as Round 3, via unquoted text; (b) counting every code span also OVERcounted a genuinely single-surface field that mentioned the same path twice or contained an unrelated inline code span (e.g. a CLI flag) in its own prose, needlessly declining a safe deterministic route. The same review round also found this exercise's three synthetic units under-populated (6 of 13 required Worker Unit Contract fields) and found this artifact's own history section had already misattributed which PR introduced which fix.

Round 5 (valid but structurally scoped; PR #403, second commit, same PR as Round 4 -- no second Codex invocation): replaced the code-span-counting check with a single whole-field anchor, `extractSoleInvokedNotModifiedPath`: the ENTIRE 'Files/surfaces expected to change' field (once trimmed) must be exactly one backtick-quoted path immediately followed by the fixed '(invoked, not modified)' phrase and nothing else (an optional trailing period aside). This closes both Round 4 gaps at once -- no unquoted second surface can hide from a whole-field match, and no per-token dedup/exception heuristic is needed for the over-strictness case, because anything beyond the bare minimal assertion (quoted or not, duplicate or not) simply fails to match and falls through to a reasoning-worker route. Combined with the pre-existing `isUnitsOwnDeliverable` check (defense in depth), and with the three synthetic exercise units completed to all 13 fields, this shipped as PR #403's merged state.

Round 6 (current; founder-reviewed scope decision, documented not further patched): Stage 2 audit #404 (on PR #403's merge) found a deeper limit still present: the route verifies FIELD STRUCTURE only (Files/surfaces names exactly one valid pre-existing script) -- it does not and cannot verify that a unit's full 'Required bounded outcome' is completely satisfied by running that script alone. A structurally valid unit whose outcome genuinely requires follow-up judgment beyond the script call (e.g. 'run this checker and close the linked issue based on its verdict') still takes this route, even though the follow-up action is real, unfinished work. This exercise's own `validInvocationUnit` outcome text ('...and acting on its verdict') had exposed exactly this gap. Rather than attempt an eighth structural fix -- which would require semantically parsing outcome prose, the per-unit judgment #294's own founder clarification says deterministic routing must never become -- the founder reviewed this specific finding and chose to document it as an explicit trust boundary in `resolveUnitRoute`'s own module comment (this route verifies structure, not outcome-completeness; a contract whose outcome isn't actually complete once its annotated script runs is a contract-authoring error this tool does not catch, the same trust already extended to a unit's State/Verification-required fields not lying) rather than keep iterating in code. This exercise's outcome text was corrected to genuinely match what the route verifies rather than overclaim it.
documented_trust_boundary: resolveUnitRoute's deterministic-script route (see its own module comment in tools/orchestration/prepare-dispatch-manifest.mjs) verifies structural truthfulness of the 'Files/surfaces expected to change' field only -- it does not semantically verify that a unit's 'Required bounded outcome' is fully satisfied by running the named script. This scenario's own positive evidence below (`valid_invocation`) is scoped accordingly: it demonstrates correct routing for a unit whose outcome text is EXACTLY script invocation with no follow-up, not a claim that the mechanism can detect or reject a unit whose outcome silently includes more.
no_real_294_occurrence: No real unit in #294's own history has a 'Files/surfaces expected to change' field naming a pre-existing script that is genuinely NOT that unit's own deliverable, annotated as invoked-not-modified -- every real unit in this plan built the scripts it named. So this scenario remains demonstrated only via a constructed exercise, not a real historical #294 occurrence.

refreshed_live_rerun.description: Re-running the real, now-fixed prepare-dispatch-manifest.mjs against the real live #294 plan, after all fixes to date (PR #393's isUnitsOwnDeliverable fix, PR #399's extractCapabilityClassLabel fixes, PR #401's original annotation fix, PR #403's extractSoleInvokedNotModifiedPath fix). No real unit's routing changes as a result -- none of the 5 real units ever used the deterministic-script route post-Round-0 in the first place.
refreshed_live_rerun.interpretation: 294-B and 294-C correctly fall through to the capability-class table ('bounded implementation worker') instead of the deterministic-script route -- genuine, valid evidence that the mechanism does not falsely claim a unit's own deliverable as a pre-existing mechanism. This is a different (related) claim from the scenario's own positive claim, demonstrated separately below.

constructed_exercise.description: The real `resolveUnitRoute` function was imported directly (never reimplemented) from the real, fixed tools/orchestration/prepare-dispatch-manifest.mjs, and run against three synthetic units constructed in-memory only -- never posted to GitHub. Each unit carries all 13 fixed Worker Unit Contract fields (Round 4's own review finding: a prior version populated only 6, a shape parse-execution-plan.mjs's required-field validation would reject if ever posted as a real comment).
constructed_exercise.interpretation: Three synthetic units, all structurally valid and complete: 'valid_invocation' genuinely invokes a real pre-existing script (ready-dispatch-gate.mjs) whose Files/surfaces field is EXACTLY that one annotated path, with its entire required outcome being EXACTLY that invocation and nothing more (Round 6 corrected this outcome text from an earlier version that also claimed 'acting on its verdict', which the route cannot actually verify) -- correctly routed to 'deterministic script: tools/orchestration/ready-dispatch-gate.mjs'. 'paraphrased_modification' genuinely intends to MODIFY an existing script (parse-execution-plan.mjs), describing that work without quoting the file's exact path in its outcome and without the annotation in Files/surfaces (Round 2's adversarial shape) -- correctly routed to 'bounded implementation worker', NOT the deterministic-script route. 'mixed_surface' genuinely invokes a real pre-existing script (annotated correctly) BUT also names a separate, real deliverable (new-feature.mjs) in the same Files/surfaces field (Round 3's adversarial shape) -- also correctly routed to 'bounded implementation worker', NOT wrongly satisfied by running only the annotated script while the separate deliverable goes unimplemented. Together these three demonstrate the mechanism correctly performs the deterministic-route behavior this scenario describes WITHIN its documented structural-eligibility scope (see documented_trust_boundary above) -- every field-structure truthfulness gap found across Rounds 2-5 is closed, and Round 6's deeper outcome-completeness limit is an explicitly documented, founder-reviewed boundary rather than a remaining defect to chase further.

honest_caveat: This scenario is demonstrated only by a constructed exercise, not a real, naturally-occurring #294 unit -- no such unit exists in this plan's real history; every real unit built the script it named. This status was revised across seven rounds -- see 'history' above for the complete, precisely-attributed record of which PR fixed and which review round found each defect. Nothing here claims a stronger result than the constructed evidence actually supports: the positive evidence demonstrates correct routing for a unit whose Files/surfaces field is structurally truthful, not a claim that the mechanism verifies a unit's full outcome is complete once its script runs (see documented_trust_boundary above, a founder-reviewed scope decision, not an oversight). This record itself was twice found to misstate its own provenance (attributing one PR's fix to another) before Round 5's version -- a reminder that even a durable evidence record is not exempt from the same independent-review scrutiny applied to the code it documents.
